scope: Static analysis for a future shrink/grow Crowd Control effect
decision: Do not expose an actor-size write from this evidence alone. Establish native scale writers, actor-lifetime restoration and collision behavior first.

claims.Finding: The common Actor constructor initializes scale XYZ at byte offsets48/52/56 and the scalar at60 to float1; offset2732 is also initialized to1.
claims.Limitations: These initial values alone do not establish a safe editor range or lifetime ownership.

claims.Finding: The transform rebuild reads Actor float2732, multiplies it by float60, scales the Actor48/52/56 vector by that product, then applies the three factors to the orientation basis through1AA7D0. It publishes matrices at64 and2056 and calls the body buffer rebuild when present.
claims.Limitations: Scale affects a shared transform; it is not proved to be a visual-only edit. Attached actors, native scripts and other transform writers need separate handling.

claims.Finding: The helper broadcasts the low float in XMM1 and multiplies all four packed float lanes at RCX in place.
claims.Limitations: Hex-Rays represents the register argument as double and some callers omit it; the assembly supplies the actual float-bit argument.

claims.Finding: The matrix helper multiplies the first three 16-byte basis vectors by the three separate float factors at RDX+0,+4,+8 and leaves the fourth vector untouched.
claims.Limitations: No validation or size clamping is performed here.

claims.Finding: Joint-transform lookup can return Actor64 or2056, or compose a model joint matrix with Actor2056. Collision-shape conversion calls this same routine.
claims.Limitations: The special joint selectors have distinct branches; this finding does not assert uniform behavior for every selector or attachment.

claims.Finding: When resource WORD+6 bit0x4000 or Actor DWORD2488 bit0x400 is set, shape conversion copies signed resource WORD dimensions at+16/+18 into output floats+4/+8 without applying actor scale, transforms the shape center via3B50F0 and13F900, then subtracts resource+14. Otherwise it zeroes the dimensions and center.
claims.Limitations: Thus scaling the shared matrix changes centers without this routine proportionally scaling radii. Other collision stages may add rules and are not all reviewed here.

claims.Finding: The actor update gate3BA7C0 suppresses transform/model work; otherwise it rebuilds the Actor transform, passes Actor2056 into the motion/model path3C6AA0, and rebuilds the other shape buffer when present.
claims.Limitations: Ordinary update supplies a potential next-frame consumer; a trainer should not call this full update blindly.

claims.Finding: The update gate is the test of Actor DWORD288 bit0x400.
claims.Limitations: This bit is one gate, not a complete player-control or stable-scene predicate.

claims.Finding: The motion/model update reads the owning Actor at motion+16, gets Actor1968, and forwards its incoming matrix argument to1A4D40 or1A4CD0 depending on blend state; it also dispatches animation events.
claims.Limitations: The function has stateful animation and event side effects. A standalone transform change does not justify directly invoking it.

next: Find script/animation/native writers of scale vector and scalar, including foreign edits.
Choose visual-only or whole-body semantics and validate body/world/hit shape behavior.
Prove conditional restoration on the same actor lifetime; never restore an old value into a new actor.
Only then add a bounded size effect and synthetic/live validation.
